parts.problem_md:
Solve the simultaneous equations.

$\begin{gathered} 8 x - 3 y & = 19 \\ 4 x + 5 y & = 3 \end{gathered}$
parts.solution_md:
**Method 1**

Multiply the second equation by 2

$8x+10y=6$

Subtract this from the first equation

$\begin{gathered} 8 x - 3 y & = 19 \\ 8 x + 10 y & = 6 \\ - 13 y & = 13 \end{gathered}$

**[M1]**

Divide both sides by -13

$y=-1$

**[A1]**

Substitute this back into any of the equations

$\begin{gathered} 4 x + 5 \times ( - 1 ) & = 3 \\ 4 x - 5 & = 3 \end{gathered}$

Solve for $x$

- Add 5 to both sides

$4x=8$

- Divide both sides by 4

$x=2$

**[A1]**

**Method 2**

Multiply the first equation by 5 and the second equation by 3

$\begin{gathered} 40 x - 15 y & = 95 \\ 12 x + 15 y & = 9 \end{gathered}$

Add the equations together

$\begin{gathered} 40 x - 15 y & = 95 \\ 12 x + 15 y & = 9 \\ 52 x & = 104 \end{gathered}$

**[M1]**

Divide both sides by 52

$x=2$

**[A1]**

Substitute this back into any of the equations

$\begin{gathered} 4 \times 2 + 5 y & = 3 \\ 8 + 5 y & = 3 \end{gathered}$

Solve for $y$

- Subtract 8 from both sides

$5y=-5$

- Divide both sides by 5

$y=-1$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: For a method to eliminate one of the variables.
> 
> **A1**: For at least one correct value.
> 
> **A1**: For both correct values.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Method 1 is more efficient as you only need to multiply one equation.

parts.problem_md:
Abdallah buys 3 cucumbers and 5 tomatoes for £14.50.

Katie buys 5 cucumbers and 4 tomatoes for £15.50.

Work out the cost of a cucumber and the cost of a tomato.
parts.solution_md:
> *Set up a pair of simultaneous equations *

$3c+5t=14.5$

$5c+4t=15.5$

**[M1]**

> *Multiply the first equation by 5 and the second by 3*

$15c+25t=72.5\,15c+12t=46.5$

**[M1]**

> *Eliminate **c** by subtracting one equation from the other*

$\begin{gathered} 15 c - 15 c + 25 t - 12 t & = 72.5 - 46.5 \\ 13 t & = 26 \\ t = \frac{26}{13} \\ t = 2 \end{gathered}$

> *Substitute the value of **t** into one of the equations to find the value of **c*

$3 c + 5 ( 2 ) = 14.5
3 c + 10 = 14.5
3 c = 4.5
c = \frac{4.5}{3} 
c = 1.5$

**Final answer:** **Tomatoes cost £2**

**Final answer:** **Cucumbers cost £1.50**

**[A1 A1]**

parts.problem_md:
Des thinks of two numbers. 
The sum of his two numbers is -6. 
The difference between his two numbers is 62.

Find the two numbers.

..................... and .....................
parts.solution_md:
> *Let one number be *$x$* and the other be *$y$*.*

> *Write the sum of the numbers is -6 using *$x$* and *$y$*.*

> * *$x+y=-6$

**[1]**

> *Write the difference of the numbers is 62 using *$x$* and *$y$*.*

> * *$x-y=62$

**[1]**

> *Solve the two equations simultaneously by subtracting one from the other.*

> * *$\begin{gathered} ( x + y ) - ( x - y ) & = - 6 - 62 \\ 2 y & = - 68 \end{gathered}$

> *Divide both sides of the equation by 2.*

> * *$y=-68\div2\,\,y=-34$

* ***[1]**

> *Substitute *$y=-34$* into one of the original equations.*

> * *$\begin{gathered} x + ( - 34 ) & = - 6 \\ x - 34 & = - 6 \end{gathered}$

> *Add 34 to both sides of the equation.*

> * *$x=-6+34\,\,x=28$

> * *

**28 and -34**** ****[1]**

equations.alt:
y equals negative 68 divided by 2

y equals negative 34

x equals negative 6 plus 34

x equals 28

parts.problem_md:
The Fraser family and the Singh family go to the cinema. 
The Fraser family buys 6 adult tickets and 2 child tickets for \$124. The Singh family buys 3 adult tickets and 5 child tickets for \$100.

Find the price of an adult ticket and the price of a child ticket.

Adult ticket \$ .....................................................

Child ticket \$ .................................................
parts.solution_md:
> *Let *$a$* be the cost of an adult ticket, and *$c$* be the cost of a child ticket.*

> *The Fraser family buy 6 adult tickets (*$6a$*) and 2 child tickets (*$2c$*) and their total cost is \$124. We can write this as:*

$6a+2c=124$

* ***[1]**

> *The Singh family buys 3 adult tickets (*$3a$*) and 5 child tickets (*$5c$*) and their total cost is \$100. We can write this as:*

$3a+5c=100$

**[1]**

> *Number the equations.*

$6a+2c=124$*  **(1)*

$3a+5c=100$*  (2)*

* *

> *Multiply all of the terms in equation (2) by 2 to make the coefficient of *$a$* the same in both equations.*

* *$6a+10c=200$*  **(3)*

* **Eliminate the *$a$* terms by subtracting equation 1 from equation 3.*

`equation`

**[1]**

> *Solve *$8c=76$* by dividing both sides of the equation by 8.*

$c=76\div8\,c=9.5$

> * Substitute *$c=9.5$* into one of the original equations.*

> * *$\begin{gathered} 6 a + ( 2 \times 9.5 ) & = 124 \\ \\ 6 a + 19 & = 124 \end{gathered}$

> * Solve this equation to find *$a$*. Subtract 19 from both sides.*

> * *$6a=124-19\,6a=105$

> *Divide both sides by 6.*

$a=105\div6\,a=17.5$

> * Write the answers to 2 decimal places, because the values are money.*

**adult ticket **$= \$ 17 . 50$* ***[1]**
**child ticket*** *$= \$ 9 . 50$* ***[1]**

parts.problem_md:
A cost to hire a minibus depends on the number of hours it is hired for, and the number of passengers. 
The cost is \$h per hour plus \$p per passenger.

i) When the minibus is hired for 3 hours with 10 passengers the cost is \$61.

Complete the equation.

$3h+10p=$............................

[1]

ii) When the minibus is hired for 5 hours with 8 passengers the cost is \$80.

Write this information as an equation.

[2]

iii) Solve your two simultaneous equations to find $h$ and $p$. You must show all your working.

$h=$................................................

$p=$................................................[4]
parts.solution_md:
i) *The cost is equal to the combination of hours and passengers stated*

**61** **[1]**

** **ii) *5 hours and 8 passengers can be represented as *

$5h+8p$

**[1]**

> *Use the same linear format for the equation as in part bi)*

**5****h**** + 8****p**** = 80**** ****[1]**

**  **

iii) *The two simultaneous equations to solve are*

$3h+10p=61$

$5h+8p=80$

> *Multiply the first equation by 5 to make the coefficients of *$h$* the same*

$( 5 \times 3 h ) + ( 5 \times 10 p ) = ( 5 \times 61 )$

$15h+50p=305$

> *Multiply the second equation by 3 to make the coefficients of *$h$* the same*

*  *$( 3 \times 5 h ) + ( 3 \times 8 p ) = ( 3 \times 80 )$

$15h+24p=240$

**Equating coefficients of **$h$** or **$p$** [1]**

*Eliminate the *$h$* term from each equation by subtracting one equation from the other*

![igcse-cie-mar-20-paper-3-q5biii](assets/001-igcse-cie-mar-20-paper-3-q5biii.png)

**Correctly eliminating **$h$** or **$p$** [1]**

> *Solve the 1-step equation by dividing both sides by 26*

$p=65\div26=2.5$

**Correctly finding **$p=2.5$**or **$h=12$** [1]**

> *Substitute *$p=2.5$* into either of the two original equations and solve for *$h$

$\begin{gathered} 3 h + ( 10 \times 2.5 ) & = 61 \end{gathered}$

$3h+25=61$

$3h=61-25$

$3h=36$

$h=\frac{36}{3}$

$h=12$

* ***h**** = 12, ****p**** = 2.5 ****[1]**

A plant costs $p$ dollars and a bush costs $b$ dollars. 
Ana buys 2 plants and 4 bushes for \$42. 
Paola buys 7 plants and 9 bushes for \$107.

Write down a pair of simultaneous equations and solve them to find the value of $p$ and the value of $b$.
 You must show all your working.

parts.solution_md:

* *$2p+4b=42$* **(equation 1)*

**[1]**

> *Form an equation for Paola.*

* *$7p+9b=107$* **(equation 2)*

* ***[1]**

> *Multiply all the terms in equation 1 by 7 and all the terms in equation 2 by 2 to equate the *$p$* coefficients.*

* *$14p+28b=294$* **(equation 3)*

* *$14p+18b=214$* **(equation 4)*

> * *

**equating coefficients of **$p$** or **$b$** ****[1]**

> *Subtract equation 4 from equation 3 to eliminate *$p$*.*

> * *`equation`

** eliminating one variable**** [1]**

> *Solve *$10b=80$* by dividing both sides by 10.*

> * *$b=80\div10\,\,b=8$

> * *

> *Substitute *$b=8$* into one of the equations.*

> * *$2 p + ( 4 \times 8 ) = 42$

> * Work out *$4\times8$*, and subtract from both sides.*

> * *$2p=42-32\,\,2p=10$

$3x=5y$** [1] **

> *Multiply equation 2 by 3 to make the coefficients of *$x$* the same.*

> * *$- 3 x + 6 y = 12 ( \text{equation} 3 )$

* ***eliminate one variable ****[1]**

** **

> * *

> *Add 60 to both sides.*

> * *$3x=0+60\,\,3x=60$

parts.problem_md:
Beindu goes to the market to buy apples and bananas.

She can buy

- 7 apples and 4 bananas for 85 cents

or

- 3 apples and 8 bananas for 93 cents.

Apples cost $a$ cents each and bananas cost $b$ cents each.

i) This information can be used to write down two equations. One of these is $7a+4b=85$. Write down the other equation.

....................... = ............... [2]

ii) Solve these two simultaneous equations. You must show all your working.

a = .................................

b = .................................  [3]
parts.solution_md:
(i) *3 apples *$( a )$* and 8 bananas *$( b )$* cost 93 cents*

$3a+8b=93$ **[2]** 
**1 mark for each side of equation**

(ii) *The two equations are*

$\begin{gathered} 7 a + 4 b & = 85 \\ 3 a + 8 b & = 93 \end{gathered}$

> *Multiply the first equation by 2, so the coefficients of *$b$* match*

$\begin{gathered} 14 a + 8 b & = 170 \\ 3 a + 8 b & = 93 \end{gathered}$

> *Subtract the second equation from the first equation to eliminate *$b$

$11a=77$

**Eliminating either variable**** [1]**

> *Divide both sides by 11 to find *$a$

$a=7$

**Either variable found ****[1]**

> *Substitute into the first equation, *$7a+4b=85$*, and solve to find *$b$

$\begin{gathered} 7 ( 7 ) + 4 b & = 85 \\ 49 + 4 b & = 85 \\ 4 b & = 36 \\ b = 9 \end{gathered}$

$a=7$ 
$b=9$

**Both variables found ****[1]**

> *Number the equations*

$5 x + 4 y = 10 \textcircled{1}
7 x - 6 y = 43 \textcircled{2}$

> *Make the **y **coefficients the same. Find the lowest common multiple of 4 and 6 which is 12.*

> *Multiply everything in equation (1) by 3 and everything in equation (2) by 2.*

$15 x + 12 y = 30 \textcircled{3}

**[1]**

> *Add the equations together to eliminate the **y** variable.*

$29x=116$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 29*

$x=4$* ***[1]**

**Extract:**

A shop sells pens and notebooks. The cost of a pen is p cents and the cost of a notebook is n cents. On Monday, the shop sells 5 pens and 4 notebooks for 450 cents. 5p + 4n = 450

Solve your two equations to find the cost of a pen and the cost of a notebook.

You must show all your working.

Cost of a pen = ...................................... cents  Cost of a notebook = ...................................... cents
parts.solution_md:
> *The two simultaneous equations to solve are*

> * *$5p+4n=450$

$10p+3n=525$

> *Multiply the first equation by 2 to make coefficients of *$p$* the same*

> * *$( 2 \times 5 p ) + ( 2 \times 4 n ) = ( 2 \times 450 )$

$10p+8n=900$

> *Eliminate the *$p$* term from each equation by subtracting one equation from the other*

$\frac{10p+8n=900\,10p+3n=525-}{5n=375}$

** [1]**

> *Solve the 1-step equation by dividing both sides by 5*

$n=75$

*Substitute *$n=75$* into either of the two original equations and solve for *$p$* *

$\begin{gathered} 10 p + ( 3 \times 75 ) & = 525 \\ 10 p + 225 & = 525 \\ 10 p & = 525 - 225 \\ 10 p & = 300 \\ p = 300 \div 10 \\ p = 30 \end{gathered}$

**Cost of a pen = 30 cents**** ****[1]**** **
**Cost of a notebook = 75 cents ****[1]**

> *Equate coefficients of *$y$* by multiplying the first equation by *$3$

$15x-6y=78\,\frac{7x+6y=10+}{22x=88}$

**[1]**

$x=88\div22=4$

> *Substitute *$x=4$* into either equation and solve for *$y$

$7\times4+6y=10$

$28+6y=10$

$6y=10-28$

$6y=-18$

$y=-18\div6=-3$

$x=4,y=-3$** [1]**
